question_text: When a high-speed signal transitions between PCB layers using a via, why must you place a "ground return via" right next to it?
answer_text: To provide an immediate vertical path for the return current, keeping the loop inductance as small as possible.
explanation_text:
The return current on the reference plane must follow the signal vertically to the new reference plane. Without a nearby return via, the current wanders the board looking for a path (like a distant decoupling capacitor), creating massive loop inductance and ruining signal integrity.

*Highly Recommended Reading: https://www.allaboutcircuits.com/technical-articles/better-pcb-design-return-paths-impedance/*
bonus_question_text: What if the signal transitions from a layer referenced to Ground to a layer referenced to Power?
bonus_answer_text: You must place a stitching capacitor near the signal via to allow the high-frequency return current to jump between the Ground plane and the Power plane.
